subject: Acme TCO post-call recap: token economics, caching, and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: TCO discussion & next steps

Hi Alex / Samantha —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our conversation and the next steps we agreed on. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Key pain points you shared:
- High per-token costs on current provider driving up support automation spend (primary concern).
- Spiky traffic with expensive peaks during support hours; budget is strict (Q2 cap).
- Need predictable per-session pricing for forecasting and procurement.

Goals we discussed:
- Reduce monthly inference spend by ~30% while preserving response quality for customer-facing assistants.
- Contain peak latency to <= 600ms for 95th percentile.
- Get an internal TCO model (ballpark) to present to finance by 3/24.

What Redwood recommends (high level):
- Prefix/KV caching + workload-aware batching to cut per-token compute (we estimated 15–35% savings depending on cache hit rate).
- Model/quantization suggestions (int8 or 4-bit where quality tolerates it) for longer sessions.
- Routing some lower-risk flows to cheaper model variants during peaks.

Action items (owners & tentative dates):
- Marissa: Send detailed usage snapshot you mentioned + our initial TCO playbook (attached) — today (attached: 20260315-acme-usage-snapshot.csv).
- Dev (cc): Provide a quick technical note on batching/caching levers and expected savings ranges — by 3/17.
- Alex / Samantha: Share any internal perf targets or cost-per-conversation thresholds — by 3/18.
- Schedule follow-up: 30-min ROI + demo session the week of 3/22 (I’ll propose times).

Attached: usage snapshot (CSV) we reviewed on the call.

Thanks — talk soon.

Hi Alex — quick technical follow-up with the levers we discussed and conservative savings estimates.

Assumptions from your snapshot: avg tokens/convo = 1,200, peak concurrent 180, typical seq len 400 per request (assistant response).

1) Batching (continuous batching):
- If we batch to avg effective batch size 8 for peak workloads, we expect ~18–25% GPU token-cost reduction (fewer kernel calls, better utilization).
- Latency impact: added queuing ~30–80ms at peak; still within your 600ms 95p goal in our tests.

2) Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts/sessions:
- With a 20–40% cache hit on conversational prefixes, token generation reduces proportionally for repeated context. Expected additional 10–20% savings depending on session reuse.

3) Quantization & lighter model variants for non-critical flows:
- Switching non-sensitive flows to an int8-quantized variant can cut per-token cost by ~20–40% with modest quality degradation on long-form outputs.

Combined conservative estimate (batching + caching + routing some flows): 30% cost reduction baseline; optimistic up to 45% with high cache hits and model tiering.

Example ROI (monthly):
- Current: 300k convos/mo * 1,200 tokens/convo = 360M tokens; at $0.000022/token => $7,920/mo (example current price).
- Redwood conservative: 30% token reduction => 252M tokens; with model/infra pricing and reserved capacity options, ballpark spend ~$5,500/mo; ~30% savings.

Attachments: I’ve added our short TCO playbook and a one-pager you can share with finance.

Happy to run a quick model with your exact pricing numbers — if you send your current per-token rate we’ll produce a short line-item comparison.
